solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Put an end to hard drink

definitions.meaning: to ... a rumour or plan is to stamp it out
whisky distilled in Scotland is a strong spirit

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses of one word: the verb for quashing a plan, and the noun for Scottish whisky.

clue.text: Company holding left-wing set of beliefs

indicators.note: the company abbreviation holds the colour inside it, like a container

parts.note: red is the colour of the political left

explanation.surface: A firm that clings to a socialist creed.
explanation.definitionFit: A creed is a statement of faith, from the Latin for I believe.

clue.text: Vulgar criminal steals set

indicators.note: something criminal is crooked or bent, so these letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A coarse crook makes off with a whole collection.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking good taste means coarse or crude, the same as vulgar.

clue.text: Bear climbing on the French fairground stall

indicators.note: in a down entry climbing means the letters read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: Pooh is A. A. Milne's famous teddy bear
la is the French feminine word for the

explanation.surface: A bear clambering up on a French article.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairground hoopla is a stall where players throw rings over prizes to win them.

clue.text: Bond villain's not half one to take tips from Smersh — he may go round in a tank

definitions.text: he may go round in a tank

indicators.note: only half of the villain's ten-letter name is used, its front five letters

parts.note: Goldfinger is the gold-obsessed villain of the James Bond novel and film
the Roman numeral for one is I

indicators.note: the tips of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A Bond baddie, only half the man, takes advice from the Soviet spy agency Smersh.
explanation.walkthrough: SMERSH was the Soviet counter-intelligence agency in Bond stories. The definition plays on a pet fish swimming circuits round its tank, not a soldier in an armoured vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A pet fish kept in an aquarium swims endlessly in circles round its glass container.

clue.text: What Faberge often did for classic advertising slogan

definitions.meaning: the jeweller Faberge crafted ornate jewelled eggs, so his job was literally labouring at an egg
a famous 1950s-60s British Egg Marketing Board slogan urging people to eat an egg for breakfast

explanation.walkthrough: The slogan was a long-running British advertising campaign promoting eggs at breakfast; Faberge was the Russian jeweller famous for jewelled Easter eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally describes crafting an egg, and was also a well-known British egg advertising slogan.

clue.text: Has fun cutting back lily-white flower

parts.note: to lark about is to play around and have fun

indicators.note: cutting the back off means losing the last letter of the word

parts.note: lily-white means pure, spotless

explanation.surface: Someone frolics among white lilies.
explanation.definitionFit: Larkspur is a garden plant with tall spikes of blue or purple blooms, a kind of delphinium.

clue.text: Place for discussion class about university

indicators.note: the school-class word goes around the abbreviation, about meaning surrounding

parts.note: a form is a class in a British school

explanation.surface: A class talking about its university.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Rome the forum was a public square for debate; now any venue for open debate.

clue.text: Sailor seen in faint nocturnal illumination

indicators.note: the sailor is seen inside the word for faint, a containment signal

parts.note: a slight or faint chance is a small one
tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman glimpsed in the dim light of night.
explanation.definitionFit: The glow given off by distant suns lights the night sky.

clue.text: Primitive weapon for lord hosting an event on grouse moor

indicators.note: the lord hosts, so holds within him, the other pieces

parts.note: a peer is a member of the nobility, such as a lord
a shoot is an organised shooting party, as held on British grouse moors

explanation.surface: An aristocrat throws a shooting party on his moorland estate.
explanation.definitionFit: A child's tube for blowing dried peas is a crude, toy-like missile launcher.

clue.text: Stern parent

definitions.meaning: the back part of a ship or anything else
used as a verb: to bring up children

explanation.definitionFit: One word means the back end, like a boat's stern, and also to raise children, as a parent does.

clue.text: Old king's regulation side dish

parts.note: Old King Cole is the merry old soul of the nursery rhyme; with the 's
a law is a rule or regulation

explanation.surface: A rule laid down by a monarch of yore.
explanation.walkthrough: Old King Cole is a figure from an English nursery rhyme.
explanation.definitionFit: Shredded cabbage salad in mayonnaise is served alongside a main course.

clue.text: Take seconds — that's more than enough

parts.note: ample means plentiful, more than enough

explanation.surface: Helping yourself to a second serving when you have already had plenty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take seconds' reads as going back for more food; Take is the definition, as in trying a taste.
explanation.definitionFit: To try a little of something, a taste or test, is to take some of it.

clue.text: Honour embracing old music producer

indicators.note: the honour wraps its arms round the letter for old, holding it inside

parts.note: the OBE (Order of the British Empire) is a British honour

explanation.surface: A veteran musician being given a royal award.
explanation.definitionFit: A double-reed woodwind instrument produces music, so it is a music producer.

clue.text: Get lost with cuddles regularly for great happiness

parts.note: beat it is slang for go away, get lost

indicators.note: taking the letters at regular intervals, every other one, from the word

explanation.surface: Telling someone to go away, then cuddling them often, makes for real joy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the second, fourth and sixth letters of cuddles: U, D, E.
explanation.definitionFit: Supreme blessedness, as in the Beatitudes of the Sermon on the Mount, is a state of utter bliss.

clue.text: Healthy fare served up by crone in make-up

indicators.note: the old woman is placed in the cosmetic, inside it

parts.note: rouge is red cosmetic powder for the cheeks
a hag is an ugly old woman, a crone

explanation.surface: Wholesome food dished out by an old woman wearing make-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Dietary fibre is food that aids digestion, considered good for health.

clue.text: Clothes-drier's to work in garden — it may be lucky

parts.note: a clothes horse is a frame for drying laundry; with the 's
to hoe is to weed or till garden soil

explanation.surface: Hanging out the washing before doing a bit of gardening, for luck.
explanation.definitionFit: A U-shaped iron hung over a door is a traditional good-luck charm.

clue.text: Ship carrying right flag

indicators.note: the ship carries the letter inside it, as cargo

parts.note: a steamer is a steam-powered ship

explanation.surface: A vessel flying the correct ensign.
explanation.definitionFit: A long narrow pennant or ribbon flown from a mast is a banner of sorts.

clue.text: Unnatural voice of latest hit

indicators.note: the words are struck and knocked into a new order, signalling rearrangement

explanation.surface: The new chart-topper is sung in a squeaky register.
explanation.definitionFit: A singer's high head voice, above the natural range, is artificial-sounding.

clue.text: Annoyed expression as celebrity makes a comeback

indicators.note: coming back means the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a star is a famous celebrity

explanation.surface: Grumbling as a famous name returns to the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of irritation, like drat or blast.

clue.text: The old lady to feel nostalgia for America

parts.note: to miss something is to long for it once gone
US is short for the United States of America

explanation.surface: A wife yearning for home in the States.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British slang for one's wife, just as 'old lady' is.

clue.text: Time to publish paper

parts.note: to issue a book or statement is to publish it

explanation.surface: A deadline for bringing out a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Thin soft paper, as in tissue paper or a paper hanky.

clue.text: Swindle gains little money for villain

parts.note: a scam is a swindle or con
P (penny) is the smallest British coin

explanation.surface: A con trick brings in small change for a crook.
explanation.definitionFit: A rascal or rogue, now usually a mischievous child, was once a real rogue.

clue.text: It's eaten? Not normally — it's drunk

indicators.note: arranged not in the normal way, the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A diner asks whether this is usually eaten, and is told it is in fact a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet aniseed-flavoured liqueur is something one drinks.

clue.text: Queen getting into food trade

indicators.note: the Queen's letter gets inside the word for food

parts.note: tuck is British schoolboy slang for food, especially sweets
R (Regina) is the abbreviation for queen

explanation.surface: The monarch enters the grocery business.
explanation.definitionFit: Barter or dealings, as in 'have no truck with', is an old sense of commerce.

clue.text: Youngster — a developing creature

parts.note: a pup is a young dog or seal, a youngster

explanation.surface: A child described as still growing.
explanation.definitionFit: The chrysalis stage of an insect is a creature in mid-development.

clue.text: It's smoked and cured each summer

indicators.note: cured suggests processed or treated, so the letters are worked into new order

explanation.surface: Bacon or fish smoked and cured every summer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tobacco pipe carved from white clay-like mineral is something people smoke.

clue.text: Overtake a golfer getting shot across top of pin

indicators.note: the scrambled letters lie across the extra letter, enclosing it
shot means wrecked or ruined, so the letters are scrambled
the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Passing a golfer as his shot hits the flag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting shot' rearranges A GOLFER into LEA...FROG, and 'across' spans those letters over the P from 'top of pin'.
explanation.definitionFit: To leapfrog is to jump over or overtake someone ahead.

clue.text: Leader in rock broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken over the air, so the word is heard not seen

parts.note: to rock is to shake or sway

explanation.surface: A rock star leading an outside broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: An Arab chief or head of a tribe or family is a leader.
